sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- Neeraj Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.

2. In terms of the FIR, it was alleged that the applicant used to talk with the informant for the last two years and was also blackmailing her on various occasion by threatening to upload the photographs on the Facebook etc.
It was also stated that she had become pregnant on account of their physical relations and in-spite of promising to marry her was refusing to marry her.
It was also stated that she was pregnant for the last eight months.

In the statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C.,
she stated that she knew the applicant for the last two years and on account of threat physical relations were formed on various occasions.

It was also stated that he had promised to marry her Panchu Alias Indrajeet vs State Of U.P Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ... on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110974929/
1

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: and was also threatened and now was refusing to marry her.
In the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., she reiterated the statement, however she stated that she was not pregnant and the fetus had died.
She also stated that she did not want to get married to the applicant.
The applicant has no criminal history and is in custody since 09.08.2023.
3. Learned A.G.A. opposed the bail prayer.
4. Considering the statement on record primarily the relationship continued in between the applicant and the victim for the last two years and the fact of pregnancy was also admitted.

Considering these facts coupled with the fact that the applicant has no criminal history and is in custody since 09.08.2023 and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail, would in any way adversely affect the trial and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

5. Let the applicant Panchu Alias Indrajeet be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No. 167 of 2023,
under Sections 376(2)(N), 506 IPC, Police Station Malipur, District Ambedkar Nagar, on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
